label: b2-check-R4
text:
Node check-R4 (4 of 6): write test cases and the check of R4. The cases: at least two that break the rule, as files in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R4/flag, and at least two that follow it, in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R4/pass; each one file of what the check reads (An assistant response or a message from the agent. Where: the agent's reply exists only inside the agent framework: its hook at the end of the turn gets it, and its transcript keeps it (a file in the agent's home)), like what the agent may really write. The check: the executable /opt/enforce/checks/R4; `/opt/enforce/checks/R4 <file>` exits 0 when the file follows the rule, and otherwise exits 1 and prints each violation: R4, where (the file and line, or the part of the text), and what to change. By the route: A regular expression that the checked text must match, or must not match. A match against the rule is a violation. What is read is part of the enforcer: a whole file, each line, only comments, a reply, the start or the end of a text. Check: a check script (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/check.py) with a regular expression; read what the rule is about (the whole text, each line, comments, the start or the end). It reads An assistant response or a message from the agent. Where: the agent's reply exists only inside the agent framework: its hook at the end of the turn gets it, and its transcript keeps it (a file in the agent's home).
Done when: /opt/enforce/fixtures/R4/flag and /opt/enforce/fixtures/R4/pass each hold at least two files; as the agent, the check exits 1 and names R4 for every file in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R4/flag, and exits 0 for every file in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R4/pass. The harness checks this when you reply.
